long_biography.plain_text:
A 35-person railway-maintenance business became Konrad Schnyder's platform for international expansion. He acquired Sersa from the family company in 1986 and moved beyond its regional Swiss work by developing new technical services and opening subsidiaries abroad. Under his leadership, the business grew to more than 1,500 employees and established operations across Europe, Canada and Australia.

Succession planning led Schnyder to a different kind of expansion. Rather than sell Sersa or take it public, he negotiated a merger with Austria's Rhomberg Rail. The equal partnership combined complementary markets and capabilities in track construction, railway equipment and maintenance. Schnyder later stepped back from day-to-day management and now chairs the group's Owner Board, focusing with his fellow owners on strategy and long-term development.
